Pd-Catalyzed Asymmetric Allenylation of Secondary Phosphine
Oxides with Enyne-Type Propargylic Carbamates for the
Construction of Chiral Allenyl Phosphine Oxides
Yujie Dong, Nianci Zhang, Fazhou Yang, Jinbao Wang, Bo Wang, Jun Liu, Bing Zheng,* Cheng Zhang,*
Leijie Zhou,* and Hongchao Guo*

ABSTRACT: Chiral allenyl phosphine oxides represent a significant kind of synthetic target with promising potential for various
applications. However, explorations toward their asymmetric synthesis remain scarce, primarily due to the competitive coordination
of phosphine oxides with metal catalysts. Herein, we report a Pd-catalyzed enantioselective allenylation of secondary phosphine
oxide for the efficient construction of a variety of chiral allenyl phosphine oxides. The success of this reaction arises from the
enhanced (bidentate form) coordination of a newly designed, fungicide-inspired enyne-type propargylic carbamate with a chiral Pd
complex. This protocol features high yields and enantioselectivities, scalability, and versatile derivatization. Mechanistic studies
confirmed the exclusion of a kinetic resolution pathway.
KEYWORDS: asymmetric catalysis, palladium catalysis, phosphine oxide, chiral allene, axial chirality
■
INTRODUCTION
Chiral allenes are privileged motifs in natural products,
bioactive molecules, and functional materials.
1
Consequently,
recent decades have witnessed significant advances in the
development of catalytic methods toward their asymmetric
synthesis.
2
As a result, a wide variety of chiral allenes bearing
diverse functional groups could be obtained conveniently
through asymmetric catalysis approaches.
3
On the other hand,
phosphine oxides that are incorporated within various chiral
scaffolds are widely used as organocatalysts and ligands for
metal catalysis (Figure 1a). Related synthesis has attracted
more and more attention.
4,5
Despite elegant progresses that
have been made in both areas, a method to access chiral allenyl
phosphine oxides remains unexplored until very recently, Ma,
Zhang, Qian, and Zhang jointly published the first Pd-
catalyzed enantioselective allenylation of secondary phosphine
oxides (SPOs) (during which we are also preparing this
manuscript).
6
Previously, Ma, Zhang, and Qian pioneered the
asymmetric allenylation of H-phosphonates (2022), represent-
ing the sole, highly valuable example of a catalytic approach to
axially chiral allenyl phosphonates.
7
This breakthrough
suggested that SPOs might also serve as viable substrates for
the concise construction of chiral allenyl phosphine oxides via
transition-metal-catalyzed asymmetric allenylation reaction.
However, SPOs undergo facile tautomerization to trivalent

leading to competitive metal coordination that suppresses

8

10

enabling efficient access to novel allenylic phosphine oxides
with P-stereocenter.
11
Despite these advances, methods for
direct allenyl C(sp

challenge.

Under typical Pd-catalyzed reaction conditions, in the
presence of secondary phosphine oxides (SPOs) and a
propargylic precursor, the coordination of the [Pd/L*]
complex preferentially occurs with the lone pair of the trivalent
R
1
R
2
P−OH species rather than with the alkyne moiety. This is
because the monodentate coordination of [Pd/L*] with the
π−electrons of the alkyne is comparatively less stable (Figure
1c). To address this, the introduction of a terminal alkene
allows for the formation of a more stable bidentate
coordination with the [Pd/L*] complex. This suppresses the
competitive coordination of R
1
R
2
P−OH, thereby enabling
oxidative insertion into the propargylic substrate and leading to
the formation of allenyl phosphine oxides.
12
This substrate
design strategy is inspired by prior work from the Ma and Guo

groups, who demonstrated that a similarly designed precursor
could generate a vinylidene−π−allyl palladium(II) intermedi-
ate under Pd catalysis.
13
This intermediate was successfully
intercepted by β-ketocarbonyl compounds to afford function-
alized 1,2,3-butatriene derivatives (Figure 1d). As proposed,
this unique π−allyl Pd intermediate can rearrange into a
σ−π−σ form, rendering it susceptible to nucleophilic attack
and enabling the synthesis of tetrasubstituted allenes.
Motivated by our ongoing interest in the design and
application of novel fungicide-inspired π−allyl Pd precursors
particularly for the construction of tetrasubstituted axially
chiral allenes,
14
we herein report a Pd-catalyzed enantiose-
lective allenylation of SPOs. This transformation utilizes a
newly designed, Vinclozolin-inspired enyne-type propargylic
carbamate, providing new access to a class of highly
functionalized, tetrasubstituted chiral allenes bearing allenyl
amide, phosphine oxide, and alkene moieties (Figure 1e). This
work differs fundamentally from pioneering Pd- or Ni-
catalyzed systems in two key aspects: (i) The strategic
incorporation of a terminal alkene group enables efficient
generation of novel, reactive chiral vinylidene-π-allyl palladium
intermediates for asymmetric construction of chiral allenes and
(ii) the implementation of Vinclozolin-inspired enyne-type
propargylic carbamates, featuring quaternary chiral centers,
enabled direct construction of tetrasubstituted chiral allenes
having phosphonyl unit.

With optimized conditions established, a range of function-
alized substrates 2 were evaluated (Scheme 1). Initial
investigation of nitrogen substituents (R
1
) revealed that
substrates bearing either electron-donating (Me, OMe) or
electron-withdrawing groups (F, Cl, Br, CN, and COOMe) at
the meta- or para-position afforded the corresponding products
in moderate to high yields (3aa−3ai, 29−90%) with
consistently high enantioselectivity (90−93% ee). It was
observed that para-substituted electron-deficient substrates
tended to exhibit lower reaction efficiency, suggesting that the
electronic properties of the amide moiety play a key role in the
transformation. As illustrated in the proposed mechanism, this
may be attributed to the amide functioning as a base to
facilitate deprotonation of the SPO substrate. Sterically
demanding substrates, ortho-chlorophenyl (2j) and 1-naph-
thyl-substituted substrate (2m), produced product 3aj (22%
yield, 88% ee) and 3am (55% yield, 64% ee) in significantly
reduced yield or ee, respectively. These results indicated that
steric hindrance in the substrate exerted a pronounced negative
effect on the efficiency and stereocontrol of the reaction. 3,4-
Dimethylphenyl substrate 2k performed well to provide
product 3ak in 83% yield with 92% ee, contrasting sharply
with the performance of its dichlorophenyl analogue 2l (its

proved to be unreactive. Variations of Ar groups were also
investigated. Similar to the situation of R

substituted substrate 2u exhibited good reactivity but

2, para-substituted diarylphosphine oxides bearing electron-

83%) with good enantioselectivity (73−91% ee). Unfortu-
nately, the para-bromophenyl-substituted substrate (1f) did
not give the desired product, possibly due to the competitive
oxidative insertion of the Pd complex into aryl bromide. It is
noteworthy that the para-biphenyl-substituted substrate 1g
displayed satisfactory reactivity and stereoselectivity in this
reaction, affording product 3ga in 64% yield with 95% ee. In
addition, sterically encumbered substrates including bis(3,5-
dimethylphenyl) (1h), bis(3,5-di-tert-butylphenyl)phosphine
oxides (1i), and 2-naphthyl derivative 1j proved viable,
yielding products 3ha (63%, 93% ee), 3ia (49%, 94% ee),
and 3ja (60%, 90% ee) in good yields and excellent ee,
respectively. Dialkylphosphine oxides, such as ethyl (1o) and
cyclohexyl (1p), were found to be incompatible substrates.
Phosphite substrates 1k−1n were also tested in the current
protocol, which exhibited limited compatibility: only diethyl
(1k) and diisopropyl phosphites (1l) afforded 3ka and 3la
with diminished yields and enantioselectivities.
Building upon successful axial chirality control, we
investigated whether P-chirality could be simultaneously
controlled by using diarylphosphine oxides with different
substituents (Scheme 3). Under standard reaction conditions,
2-naphthyl phenyl phosphine oxide 1q reacted with various
alkenyl propargylic carbamates 2 to afford products 3qa−3qs
smoothly, but with generally poor diastereoselectivities.
Among these, carbamate substrates bearing electron-donating
groups displayed high to excellent enantioselectivity, whereas
those with electron-withdrawing groups showed marginally
affected ee values.
Furthermore, a scaled-up reaction of product 3aa was
performed to examine the utility of this protocol. As shown in
Scheme 4a, the 1 mmol scale of the reaction proceeded
smoothly, affording 3aa in 92% yield with 90% ee. Both yield
and enantioselectivity remained at high levels, demonstrating
feasibility for large-scale production of chiral allenyl phosphine
oxides. To establish the synthetic utility of the products, their
further transformations were also explored. For instance, cross-
metathesis of 3ae with tert-butyl acrylate under catalysis of the
Grubbs-Hoveyda II catalyst generated the tert-butoxyl ester-
substituted product 4 in 66% yield with 49% ee (Scheme 4b).
Subsequently, treatment of 3ae (92% ee) with nitrile oxide or
N-phenylbenzohydrazonoyl chloride both underwent [3 + 2]
cycloadditions efficiently (Scheme 4b), giving product 5 (93%
yield, 2:1 dr, 94% and 95% ee) and product 6 (80% yield, 1.5:1
dr, 91% and 91% ee), respectively. In a mechanistic
investigation, a kinetic resolution experiment of 2a produced
3aa in 71% yield with 90% ee, and the recovered 2a showed
only 5% ee, revealing that no obvious kinetic resolution
occurred in this process (Scheme 4c).
Subsequently, to probe the essence of the terminal alkene
group in alkenyl propargylic carbamates, variants of substrate 2
were synthesized and evaluated in the current reaction. As
shown in Scheme 5, under standard reaction conditions,
propargylic carbamate 2v provided only a trace amount of
product as a racemate. The n-hexyl- and phenyl-substituted
carbamates 2w and 2x showed unreactivity, and no desired
allenylation products were detected. These results suggested
that the terminal alkene group of carbamate 2 played a key role
in this reaction.
Based on the results of kinetic resolution experiments and
substrate scope investigations of compound 2, a plausible
reaction mechanism for the Pd-catalyzed allenylation was
proposed (Scheme 6). Initially, the Pd(0) precursor
coordinates with ligand L6 to form chiral Pd(0) complex I.
This complex then engages the π-system of 2a through a stable
bidentate coordination involving both the alkyne and alkene
moieties, affording intermediate II. Although the tautomeric

■
CONCLUSIONS
In conclusion, we have developed a novel fungicide-inspired
vinylidene−π−allyl palladium precursor that enables highly
enantioselective allenylation of secondary phosphine oxides
(SPOs), allowing efficient construction of axially chiral allenyl
phosphine oxides in high yields with satisfactory enantiose-
lectivities. Notably, the resulting chiral allene products feature
two coordinating elements and a hydrogen-bonding site,
highlighting their potential as versatile candidates for use as
chiral catalysts and ligands. A key factor contributing to the
success of this transformation is the enhanced bidentate
coordination of the enyne-type propargylic carbamates with
the chiral Pd complex. This interaction is sufficiently stable to
outcompete the coordination of the trivalent tautomer of the
SPOs, offering a promising strategy to overcome challenges
associated with strongly coordinating substrates, such as
pyridine-containing analogues in asymmetric Pd catalysis.
Further mechanistic investigations and applications of this
novel vinylidene−π−allyl palladium precursor are currently
underway in our laboratory.

ABSTRACT: Chiral allenyl phosphine oxides represent a significant kind of synthetic target with promising potential for various
applications. However, explorations toward their asymmetric synthesis remain scarce, primarily due to the competitive coordination
of phosphine oxides with metal catalysts. Herein, we report a Pd-catalyzed enantioselective allenylation of secondary phosphine
oxide for the eficient construction of a variety of chiral allenyl phosphine oxides. The success of this reaction arises from the
enhanced (bidentate form) coordination of a newly designed, fungicide-inspired enyne-type propargylic carbamate with a chiral Pd
complex. This protocol features high yields and enantioselectivities, scalability, and versatile derivatization. Mechanistic studies
confirmed the exclusion of a kinetic resolution pathway.
KEYWORDS: asymmetric catalysis, palladium catalysis, phosphine oxide, chiral allene, axial chirality
■ INTRODUCTION

Chiral allenes are privileged motifs in natural products,
bioactive molecules, and functional materials.<sup>1</sup> Consequently,
recent decades have witnessed significant advances in the
development of catalytic methods toward their asymmetric
synthesis.<sup>2</sup> As a result, a wide variety of chiral allenes bearing
diverse functional groups could be obtained conveniently
through asymmetric catalysis approaches.<sup>3</sup> On the other hand,
phosphine oxides that are incorporated within various chiral
scafolds are widely used as organocatalysts and ligands for
metal catalysis (Figure 1a). Related synthesis has attracted
more and more attention.<sup>4,5</sup> Despite elegant progresses that
have been made in both areas, a method to access chiral allenyl
phosphine oxides remains unexplored until very recently, Ma,
Zhang, Qian, and Zhang jointly published the first Pd-
catalyzed enantioselective allenylation of secondary phosphine
oxides (SPOs) (during which we are also preparing this
manuscript).<sup>6</sup> Previously, Ma, Zhang, and Qian pioneered the
asymmetric allenylation of H-phosphonates (2022), represent-
ing the sole, highly valuable example of a catalytic approach to
axially chiral allenyl phosphonates.<sup>7</sup> This breakthrough
suggested that SPOs might also serve as viable substrates for
the concise construction of chiral allenyl phosphine oxides via
transition-metal-catalyzed asymmetric allenylation reaction.
However, SPOs undergo facile tautomerization to trivalent

R<sup>1</sup>R<sup>2</sup>P−OH species more readily than H-phosphonates,
leading to competitive metal coordination that suppresses
the desired allenylation pathway (Figure 1b).<sup>8</sup> To address this,
several elegant strategies were developed to avoid the
involvement of trivalent R<sup>1</sup>R<sup>2</sup>P−OH species. Guo presented
a Ni-catalyzed O-propargylation/Horner-Mark cascade to
construct chiral allenyl phosphine oxides directly.<sup>9</sup> Meanwhile,
Zhang developed a Ni-catalyzed asymmetric S 2′ functional-
ization of phosphines, with subsequent oxidation delivering
chiral allenyl phosphine oxides.<sup>10</sup> He reported an asymmetric
synergistic Pd/Co-catalyzed hydrophosphinylation of enynes
using a newly designed masked phosphinylating reagent,
enabling eficient access to novel allenylic phosphine oxides
with P-stereocenter.<sup>11</sup> Despite these advances, methods for
direct allenyl C(sp<sup>2</sup>)−P bond construction remain highly
sought-after yet scarce, presenting a persistent synthetic
challenge.
